# ICP-002: Engineering Manager at Pre-Series-B (Secondary, Lower Fit)

## Headline definition
Engineering Manager (not VPE) at Pre-Series-B startups (20-50 engineers) — secondary segment with lower buying authority but adjacent JTBD.

## Decision cards

### [DEC-021] ICP-002 definition

**Decision:** Secondary ICP is Engineering Manager at Pre-Series-B (20-50 engineers). Lower buying authority than ICP-001 but similar JTBD.

**Confidence:** Medium (only 5 interview data points; smaller cohort).
**Evidence grade:** C (limited customer count for this segment).
**Source basis:** Research-backed but provisional.

**Commercial-bias flag:** None.

**Asset / channel / metric bindings:**
- Channel implications: lower-budget channels (founder content > paid).
- KPIs: trial signups from ICP-002-matching companies, but de-prioritized in budget allocation.

**Kill criterion:** 12 months sustained <10 trial signups + >40% churn at 3 months → deprecate as ICP.
**Reversal trigger:** Material expansion of segment (Pre-Series-B reaches 200+ companies in our market).
**Test window:** 12 months.

**Anti-pattern to avoid:** Treating ICP-002 as primary — lower buying authority means longer sales cycles + budget pressure.

**Cross-cites consumed:** DEC-001, DEC-008.

## Customer language (verbatim)

> "I want to push back on PagerDuty pricing but I don't have CFO sign-off authority."
> — Interview JT-024, 2026-03-28

## Channel signals
- Primary: founder content (LinkedIn + Hacker News).
- Skip paid acquisition (CAC won't fit ACV).

## What we are intentionally NOT doing
- Building separate paid campaigns for ICP-002.
- Treating ICP-001 + ICP-002 as one mega-ICP (different buying authority).

## Sources and basis
- 5 JTBD interviews with EM-level buyers.
- V3 Marketing Guide §2.4 (Revella 5 Rings).
- Evidence grade C.
